summary: Extends the IMAP LIST command so a client can ask for the rights the logged-in user has on each mailbox, in the same response as the usual LIST information. This saves separate requests for access rights.

eli5.summary: When you list the rooms in a building, you also learn which ones your key can open, all in one answer.

questions: how to get mailbox permissions with imap list
how to get mailbox rights with imap list
what does return myrights do in imap
which rfc defines the imap myrights command
subtitle: One IMAP LIST command can now return each mailbox together with the rights you hold on it.

tldr.problem: An IMAP client that wants to know what a user may do in each mailbox has to LIST the mailboxes and then send a separate MYRIGHTS command for every one it finds.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8440 adds a MYRIGHTS return option to the extended LIST command, so the server sends an untagged MYRIGHTS response after the LIST response for each matching mailbox.
tldr.outcome: Clients save round trips and bandwidth, and servers advertise support with the LIST-MYRIGHTS capability. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted.

today: RFC 8440 is a Proposed Standard published in August 2018. The metadata shows it has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Why Ask for Rights During LIST
sections.content:
IMAP clients typically fetch the set of rights granted on mailboxes so they can show the user only the functions that are allowed. Today the client must issue a LIST or LSUB command to list the available mailboxes, followed by a MYRIGHTS command for each mailbox found.

The MYRIGHTS command comes from RFC 4314. Sending many of them wastes bandwidth and can hurt performance if the client does not pipeline the requests.
sections.eli5: Instead of walking down the hall and asking about each door one at a time, you get the list of doors and what your key opens in one go.

sections.title: The MYRIGHTS Return Option
sections.content:
The document adds a new MYRIGHTS return option to the extended LIST command of RFC 5258. Servers that support it advertise the capability string LIST-MYRIGHTS.

For each listable mailbox that matches the list pattern and selection options, the server MUST return an untagged LIST response and SHOULD also return an untagged MYRIGHTS response with the rights granted to the logged-in user.

The order matters in one way only: the server MUST NOT send a MYRIGHTS response for a mailbox before it has sent the LIST response for that mailbox. If the server cannot look up the rights for a mailbox, it simply sends no MYRIGHTS reply for it.
sections.eli5: For every door on the list, the librarian tells you its name first and then which keys work on it. If she cannot find out, she just skips that part.

sections.title: Worked Examples
sections.content:
In the first example the client sends LIST "" % RETURN (MYRIGHTS). The server answers with LIST and MYRIGHTS lines for INBOX and foo. The bar mailbox does not exist, so it is marked \NonExistent and gets no MYRIGHTS reply.

In the second example the client uses LIST (SUBSCRIBED RECURSIVEMATCH). The server returns a LIST reply for foo because it has matching children, but no MYRIGHTS reply, because foo itself does not match the selection criteria.
sections.eli5: If a room is not really there, or is only listed because something inside it matched, you get no key information for it.

sections.title: Formal Syntax
sections.content: The syntax is written in the augmented Backus-Naur Form of RFC 5234, and terms not defined here come from RFC 5258. The whole addition is one rule that extends the existing return-option with the literal "MYRIGHTS".
sections.eli5: The grammar book gets one new word added to the list of things you can ask for.

sections.title: Security and Privacy
sections.content:
On top of the concerns in RFC 4314, the extension makes it a bit easier for a client to overload the server by asking for rights on a large number of mailboxes. The RFC notes that existing clients already do this by sending many MYRIGHTS commands.

While serving big lists, a server needs to make sure it can still serve other IMAP connections and yield execution to them when necessary. The privacy section adds nothing new beyond RFC 4314. Client authors are told that generating many MYRIGHTS responses may be expensive for the server, so clients SHOULD use a suitable match pattern or selection option to limit the mailboxes returned.
sections.eli5: Asking about every door at once makes the librarian work hard, so ask only about the doors you care about.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: Two registrations are made. The LIST-MYRIGHTS capability is added to the IMAP Capabilities registry. The MYRIGHTS option is added to the LIST-EXTENDED options registry as a RETURN option, with the description that it causes the LIST command to return MYRIGHTS responses in addition to LIST responses. Its intended usage is COMMON.
sections.eli5: The new feature gets its name written in the official list so nobody else uses it for something different.

data.title: LIST with RETURN (MYRIGHTS)
data.code:
C: A01 LIST "" % RETURN (MYRIGHTS)
S: * LIST () "." "INBOX"
S: * MYRIGHTS "INBOX" lrswipkxtecda
S: * LIST () "." "foo"
S: * MYRIGHTS "foo" lrs
S: * LIST (\NonExistent) "." "bar"
S: A01 OK List completed.
